checks: Checked original note 5dd0d34dec315bd7, §§1–3, (1)–(4). The normalized quantile is v/a, the common cut threshold is -1, and the far-tail threshold is 2.

The height has a nondegenerate compact range because A is full-dimensional and the height is nonzero. The segment through two extreme-level points gives an affine selector in every actual section. The deviations in x and y have opposite signs and the same absolute value, at most the x-coordinate width W.

The height has an atomless strictly increasing distribution on its range. The interior quantile has lower area exactly v. If a selector has nonpositive slope and value strictly above -1+W there, a positive extra interval of captured sections pushes its cap area above v. If the slope is positive and the value is at least -1+W, every section above the quantile is captured and has area a-v>v. The arguments allow a zero slope and equality in the nonpositive-slope case. Using the smaller cap for X and the cap of area v for Y yields the same bound at one common level.

Adding the selector bounds gives t_*≥2-2W. This remains valid when the proposed lower-cap threshold is below the support. The width is attained by compactness of equal-height point pairs and is positive. Minkowski interpolation of the interval sections gives concavity. A triangular lower envelope based on the maximum integrates to W(h-ell)/2, with one triangular piece absent when the maximum occurs at an endpoint.

The coordinate change has absolute determinant one. The strip from 2-2W to 2 has length 2W and cross-width at most W, so its area is at most 2W². The boundary line at 2 has zero area. A proper t=-1 cut gives ell<-1<h and thus h-ell>H>0, making the width bound strict and yielding the coefficient 8 in the weakened tail estimate.

overlap.comparison: Its three-cap cover formula can be applied to x≥-1, y≥-1, t≥2 and gives a tail lower bound involving min(u, tail). This lemma gives a different width-dependent estimate and a common lower quantile for the actual sections, which are absent from that formula.

Uses the three-cap cover formula to control the far tail under a particular mixed-body hypothesis and a specified ordering of attained caps. It does not give the common-quantile bound or the dependence on a section width of an arbitrary planar body.

readability: W is a coordinate width in the t sections, rather than Euclidean length along the line. The absolute determinant one is what makes its height integral the original area.
